description: Deterministic, closed-form baseline. The remaining scoring margin is modeled as normal with standard deviation proportional to sqrt(seconds remaining), plus a drift term for pregame strength that decays linearly with time remaining. P(win) = Phi((margin + drift) / sigma), clamped to (0.001, 0.999).
inputs: CanonicalGameState (README §7.5). The model never consumes image pixels.
features: score differential (team score minus opponent score)
seconds remaining (derived from period and clock_seconds)
home-court indicator (default drift when no pregame prior is supplied)

optional_features.name: pregame prior
optional_features.default: not used (neutral; home edge applies instead)
optional_features.mechanism: The team's pregame win probability p in (0,1) is converted to an equivalent full-game point spread, probit(p) * full_game_margin_sd, and applied as drift scaled by the fraction of the game remaining — the same mechanism as the home edge, which it replaces (a market- or rating-derived prior already prices in the venue). The effect decays to zero as time expires.

optional_features.name: possession
optional_features.mechanism: Only when the flag is true AND state.possession_team_id is non-null: the team with the ball gets +0.6 points of effective margin (its opponent -0.6). OFF by default per README §7.6 — add possession only if it is reliably extracted from the broadcast.

overtime_handling.seconds_remaining: For period >= 5, only the current 5-minute overtime period counts: seconds remaining = clock_seconds, clamped to [0, 300]. A tie at 0:00 of any period (regulation or OT) returns roughly the pregame prior, shrunk to a small edge, because another period follows.
overtime_handling.invalid_clocks: clock_seconds outside [0, period length] (e.g. OCR noise reporting 6:12 during OT) is clamped rather than rejected. Plausibility enforcement belongs to the game-state reconciler (README §7.5); the engine stays total and deterministic.

assumptions: Scoring margin evolves like Brownian motion: independent increments, variance linear in elapsed time, no clustering by possession or foul-game dynamics.
One volatility constant (11.5 points full-game margin sd) fits all NBA matchups, eras, and pace profiles.
Home-court advantage is a constant 2.5 points over a full game, decaying linearly with time remaining.
A supplied pregame prior fully subsumes home-court advantage.
Overtime play has the same per-second scoring volatility as regulation.
known_limitations: Uncalibrated: no historical evaluation has been run. Mid-range probabilities (55-85%) are the most likely to be miscalibrated.
End-game tactics (intentional fouling, clock management, garbage time) violate the Brownian assumption, so very-late-game probabilities for 4-8 point leads are approximate.
The flat +0.6-point possession adjustment is amplified as sigma shrinks near 0:00; with the flag on, a tied game with seconds left and the ball reads stronger than reality.
No inputs for team strength beyond the optional scalar prior: injuries, rest, lineups, and fouls are unmodeled.
The clamp to (0.001, 0.999) means the model never expresses certainty, even for decided games.

calibration.note: No calibration results exist for this model version. Do not present calibration claims until scripts/evaluate-model.js has been run against real historical play-by-play data and the results are recorded here.
calibration.procedure: The harness computes the model's home-win probability for every historical state snapshot, buckets predictions into deciles, and reports predicted vs. observed home-win frequency per bucket plus Brier score and log loss. Well-calibrated buckets sit near the diagonal. If systematic bias appears, adjust full_game_margin_sd_points (spread of the predictions) or home_edge_points (level), re-run, and record the results and data provenance in this file under a new model_version.

csv_format.description: UTF-8 CSV with a header row; one row per sampled game-state snapshot from a completed NBA game. Snapshots from the same game share the same outcome label.

required_columns.clock_seconds: number, seconds remaining in the period
required_columns.home_won: 1 if the home team won the game, else 0

optional_columns.home_pregame_prob: home team's pregame win probability in (0,1); when present it is passed as the pregame prior
optional_columns.possession: 'home', 'away', or empty; when present the harness also scores the possession-adjusted variant
